benefits.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption
benefits.description: Under AS 29.45.030(e), Alaska provides a mandatory property tax exemption on the first $150,000 of assessed value for the primary residence of a veteran with a service-connected disability rated 50% or more. The exemption is administered at the municipal level: the exact application process, deadlines, and any additional local exemption beyond the $150,000 state minimum (municipalities may increase it under AS 29.45.050) are set by each municipality's tax assessor's office. A current VA disability letter (dated within the past year) confirming at least a 50% service-connected rating is required. The exemption may transfer to a surviving spouse who is at least 60 years old.
benefits.value: Exemption on the first $150,000 of assessed value of the primary residence

otherReqs: Property must be owned and occupied as primary residence/permanent place of abode
Current VA disability letter (dated within one year) confirming at least 50% service-connected disability
Apply through the local municipal tax assessor's office; deadlines and additional exemption amounts set locally
May transfer to a surviving spouse age 60 or older

application.agency: Alaska Department of Military and Veterans Affairs / municipal tax assessors
documentation: Current VA disability rating letter (within one year) confirming 50%+ service-connected disability

benefits.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate
benefits.description: Alaska issues a Disabled Veteran license plate at no cost to veterans with a combined service-connected disability rating of 50% or more, verified by a notice from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Two versions exist: one without parking privileges (VA disability notice only) and one with disabled-parking privileges, which additionally requires Form 861 medical certification of a permanent disability. Applications are submitted online through the Alaska DMV.
benefits.value: Free license plate (no issuance or renewal fee)

otherReqs: VA notice confirming combined service-connected disability rating of 50% or more
Version with disabled-parking privileges additionally requires Form 861 medical certification of permanent disability

documentation: Notice from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs confirming 50%+ combined service-connected disability rating

benefits.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting, Sport Fishing & Trapping License
benefits.description: Alaska resident veterans certified 50% or more disabled by the VA may obtain a complimentary permanent identification card allowing them to hunt, sport fish, and trap statewide, issued by the Alaska Department of Fish and Game. Applicants must be physically present in Alaska to apply and must submit a letter of disability certification. Cardholders are not required to purchase a king salmon stamp or state conservation stamp. The card becomes void immediately if the holder is no longer an Alaska resident. Anglers pursuing species with annual harvest limits must also obtain a free Sport Fishing Harvest Record Card.
benefits.value: Free permanent hunting/sport fishing/trapping license; no king salmon stamp or conservation stamp fee

otherReqs: Must meet Alaska Department of Fish and Game's residency definition
Must be physically present in Alaska to apply
Letter of disability certification submitted by email, fax, or mail to the Licensing Section
Card void immediately upon loss of Alaska residency

application.agency: Alaska Department of Fish and Game

benefits.name: State Employment Veterans' Preference
benefits.description: Alaska provides tiered hiring preference points for state employment under AS 39.25.159(a) and (c): non-disabled veterans and National Guard members receive 5 preference points (5% of total points in numerical-rating systems), while disabled veterans and former prisoners of war receive 10 preference points (10%). Ten-point veterans must be offered an interview for all open competitive vacancies open to all Alaska residents (this guarantee does not extend to department-wide or state-wide recruitment pools). Where numerical ratings aren't used, a disabled veteran or POW is given an opportunity to interview. Selected applicants must provide DD-214, DD-215, or VA documentation to verify eligibility.
benefits.value: 10 preference points (disabled veterans/POWs) or 5 preference points (other veterans) added to competitive hiring scores; guaranteed interview for 10-point veterans on open-competitive vacancies

otherReqs: Must meet minimum qualifications for the position
Applies to open-competitive vacancies for all Alaska residents, not internal promotions/transfers or department-wide/state-wide pools
Selected applicants must provide DD-214, DD-215, or VA documentation

application.agency: State of Alaska Division of Personnel & Labor Relations
documentation: VA documentation of disability rating (for 10-point preference)

benefits.name: University of Alaska Resident Tuition for Veterans
benefits.description: The University of Alaska Board of Regents (approved June 2009) grants in-state/resident tuition rates, rather than non-resident rates, to veterans eligible for VA education benefits and to active-duty service members, National Guard/Reservists, and their spouses and dependent children, across all UA system campuses (UAA, UAF, UAS). VA students who have not resided in Alaska for the prior 12 months must submit an Application for Resident Tuition Assessment (Option C) along with a Certificate of Eligibility or Statement of Benefits from the VA.
benefits.value: In-state/resident tuition rate instead of non-resident tuition

otherReqs: Veteran must be eligible for VA education benefits, or applicant is an active-duty/National Guard/Reservist service member, spouse, or dependent child
Applicants without 12 months of prior Alaska residency must submit an Application for Resident Tuition Assessment (Option C) with VA Certificate of Eligibility or Statement of Benefits

application.form: Application for Resident Tuition Assessment (Option C)
documentation: VA Certificate of Eligibility or Statement of Benefits (Post-9/11)

benefits.name: Alaska Veterans & Pioneers Home (Palmer)
benefits.description: The State of Alaska operates the Alaska Veterans & Pioneers Home in Palmer (250 East Fireweed Avenue Street, Palmer, AK), a long-term care facility with 79 total beds, roughly 75% (about 59 beds) reserved for veterans and the remainder available to non-veterans. Detailed eligibility criteria (age, residency duration, discharge requirements) and the full application process are set by the Division of Alaska Pioneer Homes and were not independently confirmed against an official page fetched this session beyond the facility's location, bed count, and veteran-bed allocation; applicants should contact the home directly or the Veteran's Liaison for admission requirements.
benefits.value: Long-term/skilled nursing care with beds prioritized for veterans

otherReqs: Detailed age/residency/discharge eligibility criteria set by the Division of Alaska Pioneer Homes; not independently confirmed via official fetch this session

application.agency: Division of Alaska Pioneer Homes, Dept. of Family & Community Services
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of military service (per application form referenced on department site)
